subject: physics
question_text: State the zeroth law of thermodynamics. What is its significance?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 12 Very Short Answer Question 2 (printed p.124). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked against NCERT Class-11 Chapter 12: the zeroth law states that if two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system separately, then they are in thermal equilibrium with each other; this is the principle that lets a thermometer, as the third system, be used to compare the temperatures of two other bodies.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The statement
lines: If two systems are each in
steps.margin_note: First mark. State the law for three systems, not two.
steps.why: The law needs a third system because equal temperature is otherwise only checked between two systems already in contact — the zeroth law lets that comparison be made through a separate instrument instead.
common_mistakes: Stating the law for only two systems, leaving out the third system.
Saying the two systems are in equilibrium with each other WITHOUT first saying each is in equilibrium with the third system.

recall.must_convey: That if two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system separately, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other.
accept: each in equilibrium with a third system
reject: the third system is the thermometer

steps.memory_tip: Zeroth law: A with C, and B with C, so A with B. The third system links them.

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name the thermometer as the third system.
steps.why: Two bodies far apart cannot be checked for equal temperature directly, so the zeroth law is what justifies reading a thermometer against each body separately instead.
common_mistakes: Naming the thermometer without saying that the zeroth law is what defines temperature — the definition is why a thermometer works, not a separate fact.
Saying the thermometer measures heat. It measures temperature.

recall.must_convey: That the zeroth law is why a thermometer works: it is the third system, brought to equilibrium with each body in turn.
accept: compares temperature without contact between the two bodies

steps.memory_tip: The thermometer IS the third system in the zeroth law.

insider_note: The significance is that the zeroth law defines temperature and so makes a thermometer possible; naming the thermometer as the third system is the concrete application that secures the second mark.
